messages:
maria: quick FYI — started onboarding mistral-emb-3b (baseline fp16) then ran int8 per-channel quant with our usual calibrator. seeing recall@10 down ~4% on semantic-sim holdout and silhouette score for kmeans collapsed a bit. putting raw numbers below.

jon: ugh, that's bigger than i'd expect for per-channel int8. did you run the exact same tokenization / pooling?

maria: yep same pooling (mean pooling, L2 norm). tokenizer identical. eval script: `eval/recall.py --model=mistral-emb-3b --quant=int8-perchannel --pool=mean --k=10`

kai: can you paste the metric output? also which dataset?

maria: dataset = semantic-sim-2025-small (10k pairs, balanced). output: 
```
baseline fp16: recall@10 = 0.872, silhouette = 0.41
int8-perchannel: recall@10 = 0.835, silhouette = 0.29
int8-symmetric: recall@10 = 0.862, silhouette = 0.39
```
notably int8-symmetric was much closer to fp16.

eval-bot: new run finished (id: run-20260319-43). artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/mistral-emb-3b/run-43/metrics.json

tess: interesting that symmetric did better. did you try per-tensor vs per-channel calibrator sizes? maybe calibration set too small or distribution mismatch.

maria: calibrator used 2k examples sampled from training shard A. i can rerun with 10k and with per-tensor. gives me ~30m per run. scheduling now.

jon: also check nearest-neighbor drift: are top-1 neighbors shifting to different language or tokenization artifacts? maybe quant noise pushes docs across cluster boundaries. run a quick ID flip check: how many queries changed their top-1 index.

maria: ran that too: top1 flips = 6.8% for int8-perchannel, 1.2% for int8-symmetric. so per-channel causing more reorderings.

kai: can you dump a few flip examples? curious if they're low-similarity tails.

maria: pasted three examples to thread (inline):
- Q1: "what is the return policy?" fp16 top1 -> doc_324 (semantically identical), int8-perchannel top1 -> doc_1987 (irrelevant faq).
- Q2: cross-lingual short query where candidate pool has near-duplicates; quant pulls an English short generic over translation.
- Q3: very short query (2 tokens) where L2 norm changed enough to flip.

tess: seems like small-n queries are sensitive. maybe we should force-length-aware scaling in quant step or use bias-correction per-channel?

maria: plan: 1) rerun calibrator with 10k, 2) try per-tensor symmetric int8, 3) try GPTQ-lite 4-bit on embedding layer only, 4) compute recall@k curve (k=1,5,10,50) and ID-flip breakdown by query length. will post updates.

jon: +1. also add kmeans stability test: run clustering 5 seeds, compute adjusted rand index vs fp16 clustering. that'll show structural collapse beyond avg silhouette.

maria: scheduled runs. ETA ~2.5h. if anyone wants a slot on GPU, ping me.

eval-bot: queued evals: run-44 (calib-10k), run-45 (per-tensor), run-46 (gptq4-embed).

kai: if per-tensor symmetric works reliably, we should add it as a recommended fallback in the onboard checklist (and flag model as "int8-perchannel unstable").

maria: agreed. will draft PR for onboarding docs once runs complete and we have numbers.

jon: thanks for digging in. small note: add a smoke-seed test to CI to catch >2% recall@10 drop for new model+quant combos.

maria: noted. will attach logs & example flips to PR. :mag:
